The '''2019 [[Eliteserien]]''' was the 75th <!-- completed -->season of top-tier [[Association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. This was third season of Eliteserien as rebranding from Tippeligaen.

The season began on 30 March and was scheduled to end 30 November 2019, not including play-off matches, but due to Rosenborg competing in the Europa League the final matchday was moved to 1 December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eliteserien.no/nyheter/eliteserien-og-obos-ligaen-2019-2022 |title=Eliteserien og OBOS-ligaen 2019-2022 |website=www.eliteserien.no |language=no |publisher=Eliteserien |date=8 October 2018}}</ref> Fixtures for the 2019 season were announced on 19 December 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Slik spilles Eliteserien 2019|url=https://www.fotball.no/turneringer/eliteserien/2018/slik-spilles-eliteserien-2019/|website=www.fotball.no|publisher=[[Football Association of Norway|NFF]]|language=no|date=19 December 2018|access-date=23 January 2019}}</ref> [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] were the defending champions. [[Viking FK|Viking]] and [[Mjøndalen IF Fotball|Mjøndalen]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2018 1. divisjon]]. They replaced [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] and [[IK Start|Start]] who were relegated to the [[2019 1. divisjon]].

[[Molde FK|Molde]] won their fourth title, with two matches to spare following a 4–0 home win against [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] on 10 November 2019.<ref name="league champions">{{cite web|url=https://www.tv2.no/sport/10980304/ |title=Molde er seriemester 2019: – Endelig kom det jævla gullet hjem|website=www.tv2.no|publisher=[[TV2 (Norway)|TV2]]|language=no|date=10 November 2019|access-date=11 November 2019}}</ref>

==Overview==
===Summary===
On 10 November, Molde were confirmed as Eliteserien champions following their 4–0 home win against [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] in the 28th round.<ref name="league champions"/> They won their fourth title.

==Teams==
Sixteen teams compete in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season, and two teams promoted from [[2018 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]]. The promoted teams were [[Viking FK|Viking]] and [[Mjøndalen IF Fotball|Mjøndalen]], returning to the top flight after an absence of one and three years respectively. They replaced [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] (after a two-year spell in Eliteserien) and [[IK Start|Start]] (relegated after a season's presence).

==Relegation play-offs==
{{Main|2019 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
The 14th-placed team, [[Lillestrøm SK|Lillestrøm]] takes part in a two-legged play-off against [[IK Start|Start]], the winners of the [[2019 1. divisjon#Promotion play-offs|1. divisjon promotion play-offs]], to decide who will play in the [[2020 Eliteserien]].
